how_to_read: line = exact narration. see = what happens on screen. status 'change' = the user's note is the direction to follow (it overrides 'see' where they differ). status 'keep' = build 'see' as written.

beats.line: Imagine you're Mukesh Ambani. You own refineries, petrol pumps and plastics. But you lost the one business your father dreamed of.
beats.note: The shot should start outside a big skyscrapper. It should zoom in into a window on mukesh ambani sitting on his business chair with vaults of money, cash, gold and everything surrounding him with a big logo of the ambani group written on the backside wall. On "refinery", an oil refining machine small model shows up on his desk, then on "petrol pump", a small petrol pump model shows up on his desk, then, on "plastics", a small shampoo bottle shows up on his desk. then on "lost", all the three models pop like a balloon and disappear. The whole time Ambani is sitting sulking on his chair, resting his chin on his palm.

beats.line: In 2002, your father Dhirubhai wanted a phone call to cost less than a postcard.
beats.see:
Show a miniature Indian city in 2002.
A post office and a phone booth are standing side by side and a character is looking at both of them one by one, confused which to use because of the price. The Camera then shows the character's troubled face.

beats.line: Then the family splits the empire. Your brother Anil gets the phone company, and you promise to stay out of telecom.
beats.see: There are some toys kept in a plate. Baby anil and baby Mukesh are sitting on the floor as their mother divides half of the toys between them. Anil ambani gets a phone, a power cell, and mukesh gets a small refinery toy model, and a plastic oil bottle. Mukesh tries to reach out to his brother's phone to get it, but their mother hits his hand and tells him not to.

beats.line: So you watch.
beats.note: Mukesh Ambani watches through some binoculars.

beats.line: In 2015, most Indians are online on slow 2G.
beats.note: the camera starts with a man on a palm tree, looking for network. Then the camera zooms out, and it shows a lush bazaar, all the people are holding their phones high in the air to look for signal. A huge loading bar above all of their heads.

beats.line: One gigabyte costs about 250 rupees,
beats.note: A phone recharge shop with billboard where it is written 250rs per GB, and everyone is walking past it without batting an eye.

beats.line: and every video buffers forever.
beats.note: The camera zooms to the shop owner from the previous shot's phone and his own video is loading and he looks disappointed.

beats.line: Airtel, Vodafone and Idea make their money on voice calls. So data stays a luxury.
beats.see: Three kings wearing the Airtel, Vodafone and Idea logos milk coins out of old phones, while data sits locked in a jewellery case.
beats.note: The three kinds are laughing as they drink wine swimming in piles of gold while on a hanging prison box a small tower labelled "Data" is hanging as a prisoner.

beats.line: But you see something they don't.
beats.see: Back at the chai stall, Mukesh lowers his binoculars and grins.

beats.line: In 2010, your deal with Anil ends.
beats.see: The padlock on the TELECOM door pops off and Mukesh walks in.
beats.note: Mukesh ambani as a baby is shown with another phone in his hand, showing Anil that he can now play with it too, while grinning.

beats.line: Weeks later, an unknown company called Infotel wins 4G airwaves in all 22 circles.
beats.see: At an auction, a tiny unknown bidder wins again and again as 22 pins drop onto a map of India.

beats.line: Within hours, you buy 95 percent of it.
beats.see: Mukesh fires a cash cannon that buries the Infotel guy in money.
beats.note: As the Unknown bidder is leaving the auction, Mukesh fires a cash gun and buries him in money.

beats.line: Then your daughter Isha comes home from Yale and says, "Dad, the internet in our house sucks."
beats.see: Isha's Wi-Fi router turns out to be a vacuum cleaner that sucks the half-loaded page off her laptop.

beats.line: Your son Akash adds: telecom isn't about calls anymore. It's about data.
beats.see: Akash tosses an old landline in the bin, and videos and photos burst out of his smartphone like a fountain.

beats.line: So you decide: data should be like oxygen. Cheap enough for everyone.
beats.see: Mukesh, dressed as a doctor, hands out oxygen cylinders that plug into people's phones.

beats.line: You don't fix the old towers. You build India's first 4G-only network, where even calls travel as data.
beats.see: Mukesh knocks over rusty old towers like dominoes, and shiny 4G towers sprout from the ground.

beats.line: You lay three lakh kilometres of fibre.
beats.see: He runs with a giant cable spool until the fibre wraps around the Earth seven and a half times.

beats.line: The bill: one and a half lakh crore rupees. You call it the world's biggest startup.
beats.see: A receipt prints forever, then Mukesh in a hoodie sits in a tiny startup garage bolted to the side of a giant refinery.

beats.line: On September 5th, 2016, you launch Jio. And everything is free. Calls. Data. Apps.
beats.see: On stage, Mukesh throws free Jio SIM cards into a screaming crowd and slaps FREE tags on calls, data and apps.

beats.line: Sixteen million people join in 26 days.
beats.see: A queue for Jio SIMs snakes around the block as a counter races to 16 million.

beats.line: A hundred million in 170 days. That's seven new customers every second.
beats.see: With every tick of a clock, seven people burst through the Jio store's turnstile.

beats.line: Your rivals run to the regulator, crying predatory pricing. You say their networks are dropping your calls.
beats.see: At the regulator's office the three kings cry buckets, and one literally drops Mukesh's ringing phone on the floor.

beats.line: And the insane part? You even give away the phone. The JioPhone, at an effective price of zero.
beats.see: Mukesh throws JioPhones off the back of a truck as the price tag counts down from ₹1,500 to ₹0.

beats.line: Data crashes from 250 rupees a gigabyte to under 20.
beats.see: The ₹250 price tag crashes down like a meteor, and data is now sold off a vegetable cart for ₹18.
beats.note: The same guy who we showed had 0 customers in a previous shot now has people rushing in to his shop for data and the board is changed to 18rs per GB.

beats.line: India becomes the world's biggest consumer of mobile data.
beats.see: On a spinning globe, India glows brighter than every other country.

beats.line: Telenor exits. Tata exits. Aircel goes bankrupt. Even your brother's company shuts down. Vodafone and Idea merge just to survive.
beats.see: Musical chairs: the telcos lose their chairs one by one, and Vodafone and Idea squeeze onto one seat.
beats.note: Instead of that, all the kings are crying fighting for the remaining gold coins while the cage from an older shot is empty now and a fly flies out of it

beats.line: By 2019, Jio is number one.
beats.see: Mukesh sits on the last chair, and it rises into a throne.

beats.line: Then Facebook pays 5.7 billion dollars for a slice. Google pays 4.5 billion.
beats.see: Zuckerberg, then Sundar Pichai, pull up in money trucks and each carries off a slice of a giant Jio cake.

beats.line: Today, 524 million Indians are on Jio.
beats.see: From above, a crowd standing in the shape of India lights up with phones.
beats.note: The guy in one of the older shots unable to decide between the telephone booth and postoffice is now not even paying attention to both and taking on the phone.

beats.line: Your father wanted a phone call cheaper than a postcard. You made it free.
beats.see: Back at the post office, the phone floats up off the scale, lighter than the postcard.
beats.note: Ambani from the first shot in his skyscrapper is now sitting laid back relaxed with gold piled up all around him and the data that was trapped with the three kings is now laughing and drinking wine with him while laying on a bean bag.

beats.line: That's why you call it Jio. In Hindi, it means "live".
beats.see: The red balloon from the start drifts back into Mukesh's hand, carrying a Jio phone.
beats.note: The same skyscrapper shot, but mukesh ambani winks at the camera after zooming in and sleeps.
